title: The Westphalia KPI: reconciliation cost, quarterly, operator baseline
subject: westphalia-kpi
ratio: (1) The load-bearing empirical question of the whole Part C layer is how expensive divergence repair is. (2) The operator baseline on record: approximately 3 months of human effort reconciling architecture and redundancy differences between two simple systems. (3) The measure: wall-clock hours PLUS tokens to reconcile two domain registries or two workstreams diverged for N weeks. (4) The cadence: quarterly, alongside the Part VI monitoring duty and the T-349 watch. (5) The interpretation rule: if reconciliation cost trends toward negligible, the containment architecture of Part C is over-engineered and should be simplified; if it stays expensive, Westphalia stands. (6) The metric is measurable only once two domain registries exist; until then it is recorded as not yet measurable with that reason, never as zero.
scope_conditions: the standing quarterly monitoring duty and any future report of divergence-repair cost
revisit_trigger: Revisit when two domain registries or two long-diverged workstreams first require reconciliation, or once three quarterly measurements exist
validity_conditions: only one domain registry exists, so this metric is defined but not yet measurable
